title: Minimum Total Distance Traveled
statement:
Broken robots and repair factories sit on a number line. `robot[i]` is where the `i`-th robot starts, and `factory[j] = [position_j, limit_j]` places the `j`-th factory at `position_j` and lets it fix at most `limit_j` robots. No two robots share a position and no two factories share a position, but a robot may start on a factory's position.

You choose, for every robot, whether it heads left or right. Each robot then keeps moving that way until it arrives at a factory that still has room; that factory fixes it and it stops there. More precisely:

- All robots move at the same speed, and robots never collide: robots heading the same way never meet, and robots heading opposite ways pass through each other.
- A factory that has already used up its limit is ignored, as if it were not there.
- A robot that goes from `x` to `y` travels `|y - x|`.

Return the smallest possible total distance traveled by all robots. The input guarantees that every robot can be fixed.
constraints: All values of robot are distinct, and all position_j are distinct
Every robot can be repaired (the limits add up to at least robot.length)
notes:
## Intuition

Because robots pass through each other and full factories are ignored, choosing directions amounts to choosing which factory fixes each robot, with each factory taking at most its limit. Trying every assignment is exponential. After sorting robots and factories by position, there is always a best assignment in which matches never cross: if a left robot went to a right factory while a right robot went to a left factory, swapping them would not cost more. So each factory fixes a contiguous run of sorted robots, and consecutive factories fix consecutive runs. That turns the problem into a two-dimensional DP over (factories used, robots fixed).

## Approach

1. Sort `robot`, and sort `factory` by position.
2. `dp[j][i]` is the least total distance to fix the first `i` robots using only the first `j` factories; `dp[0][0] = 0` and every other `dp[0][i]` is `Infinity`.
3. For factory `j` at `position` with `limit`, start with `dp[j][i] = dp[j - 1][i]` (it fixes nothing).
4. Let it fix the last `k` of those `i` robots for `k = 1 .. min(limit, i)`, growing `cost` by one robot each time, and keep the best `dp[j - 1][i - k] + cost`.
5. Return `dp[m][n]`.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted robots `[0, 4, 6]`, factories `[2, 2]` and `[6, 2]`. With the first factory, `dp[1] = [0, 2, 4, Infinity]` (it can take at most two robots). For the second factory, `dp[2][3]` tries `k = 1`: `dp[1][2] + |6 - 6| = 4`, and `k = 2`: `dp[1][1] + 0 + 2 = 4`. The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m · n · L) where `L` is the largest limit (at most `n`): about 10^6 steps.
- Space: O(m · n) for the table.

## Pitfalls

- Sort the factories by position too; the contiguous-run argument needs both lists in order.
- A factory with limit `0` must still copy `dp[j - 1]` forward, not leave `Infinity`.
- Totals reach about 2 · 10^11, so Java and C need 64-bit integers.
- Sending each robot to its nearest factory greedily can fail when capacity runs out.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dp[j][i]` | least distance to fix the first `i` sorted robots with the first `j` factories |
| `position`, `limit` | the current factory's place and capacity |
| `k` | how many of the last robots the current factory fixes |
| `cost` | distance for those `k` robots to reach `position` |
| `n`, `m` | number of robots and factories |

narration.2: Sort robots by position so each factory can take a contiguous run of them.
narration.3: Sort factories by position as well.
narration.6: dp[j][i]: least distance to fix the first i robots using the first j factories; Infinity means impossible.
narration.7: With no factories and no robots, nothing has to move.
narration.9: Add the factories one at a time, left to right.
narration.10: Read the current factory's position and capacity.
narration.11: Consider every count i of leftmost robots to fix.
narration.12: Option one: this factory fixes none of them.
narration.13: cost will hold the distance of the robots this factory takes.
narration.14: Let the factory take the last k of the i robots, up to its limit.
narration.15: Add the distance of robot i - k, the next one handed to this factory.
narration.16: Keep the better of the current best and earlier factories fixing the first i - k robots.
narration.20: All robots fixed with all factories available.
